public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 996

*Reference:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/996](https://www.erdosproblems.com/996)
 - [Er49d] Erdös, P. "On the strong law of large numbers." Transactions of the American Mathematical
    Society 67.1 (1949): 51-56.
 - [Ma66] Matsuyama, Noboru. "On the strong law of large numbers." Tohoku Mathematical Journal,
    Second Series 18.3 (1966): 259-269.
-/

@[expose] public section

open MeasureTheory AddCircle Filter Topology Asymptotics Finset Real

namespace Erdos996

noncomputable def fourierPartial {T : ℝ} [hT : Fact (0 < T)] (f : Lp ℂ 2 (@haarAddCircle T hT))
    (k : ℕ) : AddCircle T → ℂ :=
  fun x => ∑ i ∈ Icc (-k : ℤ) k, fourierCoeff f i • fourier i x

/-- Does there exists a positive constant `C` such that for all `f ∈ L²[0,1]` and all lacunary
sequences `n`, if `‖f - fₖ‖₂ = O(1 / log log log k ^ C)`, then for almost every `x`,
`lim ∑ k ∈ Finset.range N, f (n k • x)) / N = ∫ t, f t ∂t`? -/
@[category research open, AMS 42]
theorem erdos_996 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (C : ℝ), 0 < C ∧ ∀ (f : Lp ℂ 2 (haarAddCircle (T := 1))) (n : ℕ → ℕ),
    IsLacunary n →
    (fun k => (eLpNorm (⇑f - fourierPartial f k) 2 (haarAddCircle (T := 1))).toReal) =O[atTop]
    (fun k => 1 / (log (log (log k))) ^ C)
    →
    ∀ᵐ x, Tendsto (fun N => (∑ k ∈ .range N, f (n k • x)) / N) atTop
    (𝓝 (∫ t, f t ∂haarAddCircle)) := by
  sorry

/-- The following theorem is proved in [Ma66]. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 42]
theorem erdos_996.variants.log2 : ∀ (C : ℝ), 0.5 < C →
    ∀ (f : Lp ℂ 2 (haarAddCircle (T := 1))) (n : ℕ → ℕ),
    IsLacunary n →
    (fun k => (eLpNorm (⇑f - fourierPartial f k) 2 (haarAddCircle (T := 1))).toReal) =O[atTop]
    (fun k => 1 / (log (log k)) ^ C)
    →
    ∀ᵐ x, Tendsto (fun N => (∑ k ∈ .range N, f (n k • x)) / N) atTop
    (𝓝 (∫ t, f t ∂haarAddCircle)) := by
  sorry

end Erdos996

reformulations.difference: IsLacunary requires the multiplicative gap only eventually, allowing a finite prefix containing zeros, repetitions or decreases, unlike the positive increasing uniformly lacunary sequences in the cited papers.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every IsLacunary sequence has a positive tail satisfying the uniform gap at every index. Deleting finitely many initial summands leaves the Cesàro limit unchanged, and the Fourier-tail hypothesis is independent of the sequence. Conversely, a sequence satisfying the source's global gap condition satisfies IsLacunary. The equivalence of the universally quantified almost-everywhere convergence statements, for arbitrary f and limiting value, is proved in /workspace/review/lacunaritytests.lean as lacunary_convergence_iff; its axioms contain no sorryAx.

reformulations.difference: Matsuyama states the result for real-valued, 1-periodic functions with mean zero and L² norm one. Lean uses arbitrary complex L² functions, convergence to their mean, and eventual lacunarity.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Center and, when nonzero, normalize each real and imaginary component. Symmetric Fourier partial sums commute with taking these components; centering leaves the Fourier tail unchanged, and scaling preserves the Big-O exponent. Matsuyama's corollary therefore applies to both components for the same C > 1/2. Intersect their full-measure convergence sets and restore the mean. Zero-norm components are constant almost everywhere. Restriction to normalized real functions gives the converse. Finite-prefix invariance handles eventual lacunarity. The lacunarity equivalence was proved in Lean, but the complete normalization/complexification equivalence was not.

review.notes: Checked all three declarations. The source confirms triple-log decay in the main question and the strict threshold C > 1/2 in Matsuyama's variant. Lean experiments verified symmetric Fourier indices, the k = 0 partial sum, volume = haarAddCircle for period 1, finite Fourier-tail eLpNorm, integrability, eventual positivity of the iterated logarithms, satisfiable hypotheses, and harmless zero-index averages. Thus neither .toReal nor totalized logarithms/division introduce a defect. Scratch files are under /workspace/review; the file under review was not modified.
